handing: gate:false — nothing moves. gate:true — the leaf at gateIndex is hung on two patch fittings at the stile nearest the end of the run and swings out (toward -Z) about that stile's vertical axis; gateIndex in the left half hinges left, otherwise right.

gate_leaf.sign: + for a left-hung leaf, − for a right-hung leaf; both swing toward -Z

clip.static_variant: with gate:false the clip is flat — setOpen(t) is a no-op and no node moves

note: A frameless balustrade does not move, so nothing was invented to make it move: with gate:false, setOpen is a no-op and the whole assembly is rigid. With gate:true the run is cut for a gate bay — the base channel stops 55 mm short of the pivot line (clearing the 96 mm newel base) and the handrail 45 mm short; the leaf hangs on a 56 mm stainless newel post at the pivot line, gripped by two patch fittings whose collars ride 2 mm clear of the post, and carries its own 50 mm cap rail and saddle starting 55 mm out from the pivot. Leaf width is panel − 30 mm and the static run resumes at the neighbouring panel edge, so the leaf and its latch bolt clear every fixed part through the full 90° — the free stile travels 714 mm out. Glass is seated 5 mm off the slot floor on a setting gasket; spigots are half-shell clamps offset 1.5 mm each side of the glass, so no part interpenetrates another at any t. Finish-bearing parts (channel, cover trim, handrail, saddles) are on upvc_white_matte / upvc_white_rebate; only clamps, patches and the pull are steel or matte black.
